paragraphs.paragraph: The Leaders’ Responsibility and Israel’s Sins

answers: The priests, the house of Israel, and the house of the king
The king of Assyria only
The tribes of Judah only
easy.explanation: The prophet addresses the priests, the house of Israel, and the house of the king.
easy.q: To whom does the prophet speak at the beginning of the passage?

answers: Strong trees
A snare and a net
Fortified towers
easy.explanation: They are described as a snare on Mizpah and a net spread upon Tabor.
easy.q: What are the leaders compared to in verse 1?

answers: Ephraim and Israel
Assyria and Judah
The priests only
easy.explanation: The passage says that Ephraim committed whoredom and Israel was defiled.

answers: They do not know the land
Their deeds and the spirit of whoredoms keep them from returning
They have no sacrifices
medium.explanation: Their deeds are not directed toward God, and the spirit of whoredoms is in their midst.
medium.q: Why will the people not turn unto God?

answers: The leaders became a spiritual trap for the people
The leaders were faithful watchmen
The leaders provided a place of refuge
medium.explanation: The leaders are pictured as a snare and a net that ensnared the people.
medium.q: What does the phrase “ye have been a snare on Mizpah” mean in context?

answers: The Lord does not know what Ephraim has done
The Lord knows Ephraim’s deeds, yet Ephraim is still committing whoredom
Ephraim successfully hid its deeds
medium.explanation: The Lord says, “I know Ephraim,” while also declaring that Ephraim is committing whoredom.
medium.q: What is the relationship between the Lord knowing Ephraim and Ephraim’s sin?

answers: Only the people are responsible
Responsibility involves both the leadership and the people’s conduct
The prophet is speaking only about royal matters
challenge.explanation: The address to the priests, Israel, and the royal house highlights both leadership responsibility and the people’s sins.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the prophet addressing both the leaders and the house of Israel?

answers: The spirit keeps them from returning and knowing the Lord
The spirit helps them know the Lord better
The spirit describes fear of a foreign enemy only
challenge.explanation: The spirit of whoredoms is in their midst, and therefore they have not known the Lord.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the “spirit of whoredoms” and not knowing the Lord?

answers: Sin within, defilement, and inability to return unto the Lord
Victory, prosperity, and thanksgiving
War, covenant, and return to the land
challenge.explanation: The passage presents inner sin and defilement that prevent the people from returning to the Lord.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly summarizes the ideas in these verses?

paragraphs.idea: The Leaders’ Responsibility and Israel’s Sins

answers: It will increase
It will testify against Israel and be humbled
It will disappear into Assyria
easy.explanation: The pride of Israel will testify to his face, and Israel will fall in his iniquity.
easy.q: What will happen to the pride of Israel?

answers: Israel, Ephraim, and Judah
Assyria and Benjamin only
The priests only
easy.explanation: Israel and Ephraim will fall, and Judah will fall with them.
easy.q: Who will fall in their iniquity?

answers: Yes, immediately
Yes, if they bring more cattle
No, they will not find Him
easy.explanation: Although they go with their flocks and herds to seek the Lord, they will not find Him.
easy.q: Will their sacrifices enable them to find the Lord?

answers: They have dealt treacherously against the Lord and begotten strange children
They had no temple
They brought only sheep
medium.explanation: Their treachery against the Lord and the birth of strange children are connected with their coming judgment.
medium.q: Why will their sacrifices not help them?

answers: Their sacrifices will bring them to the Lord
They will not obtain the Lord’s help
They will find a new place of worship
medium.explanation: Their outward attempt to seek the Lord will not bring them into His favor.
medium.q: What does “they shall not find him” mean after they seek the Lord?

answers: Pride leads Israel, Ephraim, and Judah to fall in their iniquity
Pride prevents all punishment
The falling belongs only to Assyria
medium.explanation: The passage connects Israel’s pride with the fall of Israel, Ephraim, and Judah.
medium.q: How are Israel’s pride and the people’s falling connected?

answers: Sin and judgment are not limited to Ephraim
Judah escapes all judgment
Judah ruled Assyria
challenge.explanation: The verse specifically says that Judah also shall fall with Israel and Ephraim.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Judah falling with Israel and Ephraim?

answers: The birth of strange children is presented as part of their treachery
The strange children are presented as a reason for salvation
The passage makes no connection between them
challenge.explanation: The verse joins their treachery against the Lord with their having begotten strange children.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between dealing treacherously against the Lord and begetting strange children?

answers: Outward action alone cannot repair treachery against the Lord
Sacrifices always remove punishment
The people no longer believed in judgment
challenge.explanation: Their sacrifices are ineffective because their relationship with the Lord has been corrupted by treachery.
challenge.q: What central idea appears in the movement from seeking the Lord with sacrifices to not finding Him?

paragraphs.paragraph: The Alarm of War and Coming Disaster

answers: A harp and a drum
A cornet and a trumpet
A flute and a psaltery
easy.explanation: The passage mentions the cornet in Gibeah and the trumpet in Ramah.
easy.q: What instruments are they commanded to sound?

answers: Gibeah, Ramah, Beth-aven, and Benjamin
Assyria, Egypt, and Judah only
Jerusalem and the house of David only
easy.explanation: The alarm is sounded in Gibeah and Ramah, with a cry at Beth-aven and a reference to Benjamin.
easy.q: Which places and people are mentioned in connection with the alarm?

answers: Desolate
A strong kingdom
A place of refuge
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Ephraim shall be desolate in the day of rebuke.”
easy.q: What will Ephraim become in the day of rebuke?

answers: A feast and celebration
Fear, war, and approaching judgment
The end of punishment
medium.explanation: The instruments function as an alarm announcing danger and judgment.
medium.q: What do the sounding of the cornet and trumpet announce?

answers: Ephraim will be made desolate
Ephraim will be joyful
Ephraim will be anointed
medium.explanation: The word “desolate” indicates ruin and emptiness.
medium.q: What does “Ephraim shall be desolate” mean?

answers: As sudden strengthening
As gradual weakening like a moth and rottenness
As peace between the kingdoms
medium.explanation: The Lord says He will be to Ephraim as a moth and to Judah as rottenness.
medium.q: How is the punishment of Ephraim and Judah described in verse 12?

answers: They signal that judgment and disaster are becoming immediate
They remove the people’s sins
They announce that the war is finished
challenge.explanation: The cornet and trumpet serve as warnings of approaching judgment.
challenge.q: What is the role of the alarms within the passage?

answers: The punishment works gradually and weakens the kingdoms
The punishment is only outward noise
The kingdoms are growing stronger inwardly
challenge.explanation: A moth and rottenness destroy gradually, illustrating the weakening of Ephraim and Judah.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the images of a moth and rottenness?

answers: Judah’s princes remove the boundary, so the Lord pours His wrath upon them
Judah is not mentioned in the punishment
Judah receives protection because of Ephraim’s sins
challenge.explanation: The princes of Judah are compared to those who remove the bound, and judgment is poured upon them.
challenge.q: How are Judah’s sins connected to the punishment in this passage?

paragraphs.paragraph: Turning to Assyria and the Lord’s Withdrawal

answers: The Assyrian and king Jareb
The royal house of Judah
The priests only
easy.explanation: Ephraim went to the Assyrian and sent to king Jareb.
easy.q: To whom did Ephraim turn for healing?

answers: Yes, he heals both
He heals Judah only
No, he cannot heal or cure them
easy.explanation: The passage says that king Jareb could not heal them or cure their wound.
easy.q: Can king Jareb heal Ephraim and Judah?

answers: They will seek the Lord early
They will flee to the mountains
They will ask only for more sacrifices
easy.explanation: The final verse says, “in their affliction they will seek me early.”
easy.q: What will the people do in their affliction?

answers: They sought relief from their sickness and wound
They wanted to enlarge their borders
They wanted to teach Assyria the law
medium.explanation: Ephraim saw its sickness and Judah saw its wound, so they turned to Assyria.
medium.q: Why did Ephraim and Judah turn to Assyria?

answers: The Lord tears and takes away, and none can rescue
The Lord is a shepherd protecting the flock
The Lord heals the kingdoms
medium.explanation: The lion imagery emphasizes the Lord’s irresistible judgment.
medium.q: What does the image of the Lord as a lion and a young lion communicate?

answers: The people must acknowledge their offence and seek His face
Assyria must send an army
Judah must build stronger walls
medium.explanation: The Lord says He will withdraw until they acknowledge their offence and seek His face.
medium.q: What must happen before the Lord’s withdrawal ends?

answers: They rely on a foreign power instead of the Lord
They have already returned to the Lord
They do not recognize that they are in trouble
challenge.explanation: They seek healing from Assyria, but Assyria cannot save or cure them.
challenge.q: What does turning to Assyria reveal about Ephraim and Judah’s dependence?

answers: The Lord withdraws until they acknowledge their guilt and seek Him
The withdrawal guarantees that they will never return
There is no connection between the withdrawal and their actions
challenge.explanation: The Lord’s withdrawal continues until the people acknowledge their offence and seek His face.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the Lord’s withdrawal and the people’s repentance?

answers: Assyria cannot heal, while the Lord controls judgment and calls the people to seek Him
Assyria punishes while the Lord immediately heals
Assyria and the Lord are shown to have equal power
challenge.explanation: Assyria cannot cure the wound, while the Lord is the one who brings judgment and awaits their seeking Him.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between Assyria and the Lord in this passage?
